additions.reason: Central concept: the burial place of the tzaddik possesses the holiness of Eretz Yisrael. Also identified as a tikkun for pgam habrit. Hub node connecting the other two concepts.
additions.source_quote: שֶׁמְּקוֹם גְּנִיזָתָם הוּא קָדוֹשׁ בִּקְדֻשַּׁת אֶרֶץ־יִשְׂרָאֵל מַמָּשׁ

additions.reason: The burial place of true tzaddikim is identified (bechina) with the holiness of Eretz Yisrael — their resting place IS holy with the kedusha of the Land.
additions.source_quote: שֶׁהַצַּדִּיקִים אֲמִתִּיִּים יוֹרְשִׁים אֶרֶץ־יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁזּוֹכִין שֶׁמְּקוֹם גְּנִיזָתָם הוּא קָדוֹשׁ בִּקְדֻשַּׁת אֶרֶץ־יִשְׂרָאֵל מַמָּשׁ

additions.reason: Eretz Yisrael is stated to be (הוא) a great tikkun for pgam habrit — a bechina-style identification using 'הוא' language, indicating shared essential nature.
additions.source_quote: וְאֶרֶץ־יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא תִּקּוּן גָּדוֹל לִפְגַם הַבְּרִית

concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset: ארץ ישראל — the Land of Israel, whose holiness is present at the tzaddik's grave
מקום גניזת הצדיקים — the burial place of true tzaddikim, identified with Eretz Yisrael's holiness
תיקון פגם הברית — rectification of the blemish of the covenant, for which Eretz Yisrael IS a great tikkun
קבר הבעל שם טוב — the grave of the Baal Shem Tov, the specific instance motivating the teaching (too specific/narrative for a standalone node)
